Question 21(b) [4 marks]: Distinguish between voluntary and involuntary separation.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Demonstrates a clear understanding of the difference between voluntary and involuntary separation
3 marks: Demonstrates an understanding of the difference between voluntary and involuntary separation
2 marks: Demonstrates some understanding of a difference between voluntary and involuntary separation OR | Sketches in general terms voluntary and involuntary separation
1 marks: Provides some relevant information about voluntary or involuntary separation

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Voluntary separation is when an employee has chosen to leave their employment of their own accord. This could be in the form of a resignation, retirement or relocation. Involuntary separation occurs when an employee is forced to leave their place of employment because they may have breached their employment conditions, finished their contract or been made redundant.



WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: respond to the question directly using correct terms, such as internal stakeholders and human resource influences.
To improve: interpreting the question including responding appropriately to key terms
To improve: integrating examples and case studies into responses.
